mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals improved consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns when INDPRO growth exceeds 2% over three months.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth exceeds 2% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a supportive monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS and UNRATE are below thresholds but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns when RSAFS growth exceeds 5% over six months.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns when FEDFUNDS exceed 5%.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceed 5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) combined with increasing federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% and FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25%
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS increase as described but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, the hypothesis is rejected.
